The tool gives you the list of materials, the list of tools, and (for each part) several ordering choices.
Some stuff you already have (e.g. some tools, screws).
The tool also lets you contact friends if you can borrow / buy something for cheap from them.
The rest you buy.
Afterwards you receive instructions how to fix your phone.
If it worked, send a review and/or video of you fixing it.
If it hasn't worked out, you can send it to an expert.

args.text: When a process description includes a decision or activity, label the corresponding BPMN element with wording that preserves the described meaning; do not substitute a different decision or action.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing documented guideline already covers faithful labeling or offers a more specific rule.

result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
For a message event, put messageRef on its bpmn:messageEventDefinition, never on the event element itself.
Create reusable bpmn:message elements and messageRef only when communication content or shared message identity matters.
Return one complete, well-formed bpmn:definitions document and no surrounding explanation or Markdown fence.

args.text: Use labels for BPMN decisions and activities that accurately express the meaning stated in the process description, rather than labels that describe an unrelated decision or action.

trace.reason: Check whether an existing learned guideline already covers the label-semantic issue before proposing one.

result.rule: When the description states the purpose or destination of an activity: Include that stated purpose or destination in the BPMN activity label, rather than labeling only the broader action.

When the description gives an activity with multiple evaluation dimensions or optional methods, or states a completion outcome in detail: Use concise labels for the corresponding BPMN activities and events, preserving the central action or outcome without enumerating subsidiary details.

When the description states an activity or outcome and identifies its action, object, actor, or recipient: label the corresponding BPMN element with concise wording that preserves those stated details and does not substitute a different action or meaning

When the description names a distinct activity or outcome and states its action or completion condition: Label the corresponding BPMN element with the described action or outcome. Do not replace it with a broader or narrower action, or add detail the description does not support.
